text:
mike: Quick heads-up — saw a ramp last night that pushed p4d-prod into repeated KV-driven OOMs. pattern looks like lots of short sequences + aggressive prefill causing slab fragmentation and eviction thrash. can we triage?

sophia: which metrics jumped? any perf counter dumps or pprof traces? did kernel selection change on that cluster recently?

mike: posted a short profile snippet from 03:12-03:45 UTC:
```
batch_lat_p50: 28ms
batch_lat_p95: 230ms
kv_hit_rate: 0.42
avg_slab_frag: 31%
avg_free_per_slab: 48KB
decode_ms_per_tok: 0.9
prefill_bytes_per_req: 112KB
active_allocs: 12k
oom_events: 6
```

yves: slab_frag 31% is pretty high. looks like tiny allocations are scattering. are we doing per-request prefill that pins many small KV pages?

mike: yeah, prefill is the culprit on those tail requests — lots of small context prefills (<=64 tokens) but each prefill grabs multiple small buffers, then decode touches different KV pages and we end up with many partially-used slabs.

rachel: two levers: (1) per-request soft caps to limit prefill allocation footprint, (2) opportunistic local eviction (evict from same worker first) before global slab steal. also reuse small buffers from an LRU free-list instead of returning to slab free list to reduce fragmentation.

sophia: also verify if a new kernel variant was chosen that increased temporary workspace per decode. kernel_workspace spikes will exacerbate fragmentation even if KV behavior is unchanged.

deploy-bot: deploy kv-allocator-tune/v2 -> canary 10% at 03:20 UTC. changelog: reduced slab_min_alloc from 64KB to 32KB, enabled local-evict heuristic. no restarts. :white_check_mark:

yves: important: kernel workspace allocation must be bound to model variant so different kernels don't pollute the same slab pools. proposal: tag workspaces by (model_hash, kernel_id) and try reuse for same tag.

mike: agreed. for immediate mitigation I want to try this experiment:
- per_request_soft_cap = 96KB (soft, throttles prefill)
- enable local_eviction_first = true
- small_buffer_lru_enabled = true
- reclaim_watermark = 0.15 (start reclaiming earlier)
A/B: 10% canary on low-latency fleet, 10% control. monitor: oom_events, avg_slab_frag, kv_hit_rate, p95 latency.

sophia: heuristic rule suggestion: if avg_slab_frag > 25% AND prefill_bytes_per_req > 64KB then throttle prefill and favor streaming decode path. also backpressure at the batching layer: reduce max_batch_size by 20% for that worker for 60s.

rachel: I'll add runtime tracepoints for: alloc(size, tag), free(addr, tag), kv-evict(evicted_keys, reason), prefill_start/pre4ll_end, and kernel_workspace_alloc(tag, size). that'll let us correlate kernel workspace churn with slab fragmentation.

yves: one more: when we evict, prefer coalescing adjacent free ranges before handing back to global allocator. fragmentation-aware coalesce reduces future small-allocation churn.

mike: thanks. action items: rachel adds tracepoints + dashboard (oom_events, slab_frag by worker, per_req_prefill distribution). sophia wires batching backpressure toggle and monitors latency impact. yves prototypes workspace tagging and small buffer LRU. I'll run the canary and watch the canary->control diff for 2 hours. ack?

sophia: ack

rachel: ack, will post PR for tracepoints this morning

yves: ack, will spike workspace tagging PoC by EOD

mike: great — will post follow-up with canary metrics. if we still see OOMs after soft-cap + local-evict, next step is to experiment with prefilling policy: decode-first (streaming) for short contexts and prefill-only for long contexts.

mike: follow-up note: keep an eye on unit-economics — more streaming increases token latency but reduces memory churn. we need a knob to trade tail latency vs cost/oom risk.
